# account.albena.ai — Customer Portal contract (lead: Claude)

Separate Cloudflare Worker `albena-portal` at account.albena.ai. Own D1 `albena_portal`. Holds ONLY account, billing, hub-management data — never conversations, memory, camera or home data.

## Layout (each builder owns one area; do not edit others' areas)
- portal/worker/            Hono + TS Worker (skeleton + auth: GPT-6)  -> src/index.ts mounts routers
- portal/worker/src/auth/   passkeys (WebAuthn) + email magic link, sessions        (GPT-6)
- portal/worker/src/billing/ Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal, webhooks, entitlements (Sonnet B)
- portal/worker/src/hubs/   Hub pairing + heartbeat + releases                      (Sonnet C)
- portal/web/               Astro static UI, Linear style                           (Sonnet D)
- portal/docs/              customer help docs                                      (Haiku)

## Module interface
Each module exports `mount(app: Hono<AppEnv>): void` and `migrations: string[]` (file names under portal/worker/migrations/: 0100_auth_*, 0200_billing_*, 0300_hubs_*). Modules are registered statically in `src/modules.ts`: auth, billing, hubs, account.
Shared from auth: `requireUser` (sets `c.get("user")` = `{ id, email, role: "owner"|"member", accountId }`), `audit(c, action, target, meta?)` (hash-chained audit_log) and `AppEnv` (src/types.ts).
Entitlements: one function, `getEntitlement(db: D1Database, accountId)` in billing, returns `{ plan, status, active, maxHubs, billingInterval, currentPeriodEnd, cancelAtPeriodEnd, stripeSubscriptionId, source, endsAt, comp }`. `maxHubs` comes from `MAX_HUBS` in billing/plans.ts (byo 1, hub_mac 1, hub_nvidia 1, estate 5, pilot 1, none 0), unless a manual grant sets its own `max_hubs`; it is 0 unless `active` (status active or trialing, and not past `endsAt`). `plan` may also be `pilot`; `status` may also be `suspended` or `expired` (manual grants only).

**Entitlement source and precedence.** `source` is `stripe` or `manual` (staff grant: pilot, comp or a hand-set plan). A manual grant is never overwritten by Stripe events (canceled, past_due, incomplete, unknown price, deleted subscription are all ignored for it). Stripe replaces it only when a subscription becomes `active` or `trialing`; the manual grant is then archived in `entitlement_history` (kind `archived_by_stripe`). The reverse: staff cannot write a manual grant while a Stripe subscription can still bill (409 `stripe_subscription_active`); once Stripe is canceled/none they can. Implemented in one conditional UPSERT in `billing/entitlements.ts` (`applyEntitlement`, `writeManualEntitlement`).

## API
JSON, same-origin, cookie session `__Host-albena_session` (HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax). Browser writes need header `X-Requested-With: albena-portal` (and Origin, if sent, must be the portal origin). Machine routes (Stripe webhook, hub pair/complete, hub heartbeat) are exempt from that and authenticate themselves. Times are unix seconds unless noted. Errors are `{ error: "<code>" }`.

Auth
- POST /api/auth/magic/start `{email, turnstileToken}` (Turnstile action `magic_login`) -> 202 `{ok, message}` always (enumeration-safe)
- POST /api/auth/magic/code `{id?, code}` -> 200 `{ok}` + session cookie. The sign-in email also carries a 6-digit code. The requesting browser (the `__Host-albena_magic` cookie is required; a code alone is useless) submits it from `/check-email`. Errors (400, `{error}`): `invalid_code` (format), `wrong_code` (`attemptsLeft`), `too_many_attempts` (5th wrong attempt invalidates the token, link included), `invalid_or_expired_code` (no/used/expired token or missing cookie). 429 `rate_limited`. Same 15 min expiry, single-use, same session path and `auth.login.magic` audit event as the link. Code stored only as SHA-256 of `id:code` (migration 0102); never logged; not in the subject.
- GET /api/auth/magic/verify?token=... -> 303 to `/`. Single-use, 15 min, stored hashed, and bound to the browser that asked (HttpOnly cookie). Opening it on another device fails by design (see HANDOFF.md).
- POST /api/auth/passkey/register/options -> bare WebAuthn options; POST .../register/verify (raw browser response) -> `{ok}`
- POST /api/auth/passkey/login/options -> bare WebAuthn options (discoverable); POST .../login/verify (raw browser response) -> `{ok}`. The challenge lives server-side, bound to a cookie, single use.
- POST /api/auth/logout -> `{ok}`
- GET /api/me -> `{user: {id, email, role, accountId}}`

Security
- GET /api/security/sessions -> `{sessions: [{id, createdAt, lastSeen, expiresAt, current}]}`; DELETE /api/security/sessions/:id -> `{ok}` (404 if not yours)
- GET /api/security/history -> `{events: [{at, method: "passkey"|"magic_link"}]}` newest first, max 50. `at` is ISO-8601. From the audit chain; successful sign-ins only.
- GET /api/security/passkeys -> `{passkeys: [{id, createdAt}]}`; DELETE /api/security/passkeys/:id -> `{ok}` (404 if not yours). Removing the last passkey is allowed because the email link always works.

Billing
- GET /api/billing/summary -> `{entitlement: {...as above}, hasBillingAccount}`
- GET /api/billing/orders -> `{orders: [{id, plan, source, edition, carrier, tracking, shippingStatus, refunded, refundStatus, amountTotal, currency, createdAt}]}` (hardware orders; `source` stripe|manual; Stripe shippingStatus: awaiting_payment|pending_fulfillment|shipped|delivered|payment_failed|cancelled_refunded; manual shippingStatus: pending|preparing|shipped|delivered|cancelled; refundStatus: none|partially_refunded|refunded; `refunded` is true only for a full refund; staff notes are never returned)
- GET /api/billing/invoices -> `{invoices: [{id, number, status, amountPaid, amountDue, currency, created, hostedInvoiceUrl, pdf}]}`
- POST /api/billing/checkout `{plan: "byo"|"hub_mac"|"hub_nvidia"|"estate", interval: "monthly"|"annual"}` -> `{url}` (estate: 400 `contact_sales`; unconfigured price: 503; a subscription that can still bill, or another checkout in progress: 409; one open checkout per account, same plan reuses it)
- POST /api/billing/portal -> `{url}`
- POST /api/stripe/webhook (Stripe-Signature over the raw body)

Hubs
- POST /api/hubs/pair/start (owner) -> `{code, expiresAt}`; 402 when the plan has no free hub slot. `pair/complete` re-checks entitlement and slot count atomically with consuming the code (402 and the code stays unused otherwise); public key and signatures must be canonical padded base64
- POST /api/hubs/pair/complete (hub) `{code | serial | licenseKey, hubPublicKey, edition, profile, version}` (exactly one credential) -> `{hubId}`. `code` is the pairing code from the portal. `serial` binds a staff pre-provisioned (reserved) Hub: single use, the edition must match, expires (default 60 days), still needs an active entitlement with a free slot, and binds only the key staff recorded when they pinned one (a serial is an identifier, not a secret, so pin the key when it is known). `licenseKey` (`ALB-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX`, BYO accounts only) is reusable while a Hub slot is free and until revoked. All three share the rate limits and the atomic entitlement/slot check; the audit event is `hub.pair.complete` with `via` code|serial|license_key. No token: the hub keeps an Ed25519 key and signs every later request (`X-Hub-Id`, `X-Hub-Timestamp`, `X-Hub-Signature`).
- POST /api/hubs/heartbeat (hub, signed) `{version, profile, updateChannel, health, stats?}` -> `{ok, updateChannel, remoteAccess}`. Body cap 16 KB (413 above). `health.services` entries are `[name, status]` or `[name, status, uptime_s]`. Optional `stats` (strict allowlist, unknown keys and out-of-range values are 400; there is no free text, only bounded names and enums). EVERY field of `stats` and of its sub-objects is optional (a Hub reports only what it knows; the UI shows an em dash, never 0, for missing values): `uptime_s` int, `cpu_pct` 0-100, `load1`, `mem_used_mb`/`mem_total_mb` int (used <= total), `disk_used_gb`/`disk_total_gb` (used <= total), `temp_c`, `gpu: [{name<=64, util_pct, mem_used_mb, mem_total_mb, temp_c?}]` (<=4), `services: [[name<=32, "ok"|"down"|"degraded", uptime_s?]]` (<=24), `ai: {mode: "local"|"local+cloud", models: [{lane: fast|general|brain|code|vision|embed|other, name<=64, loaded}] (<=12), avg_latency_ms}`, `activity: {requests_24h, requests_7d, wakes_24h, approvals_pending, approvals_24h}` (counts only; conversation content never leaves the Hub), `updates: {latest_known, last_result: ok|rolled_back|failed|none, last_at}`, `connectors: [...]` (see "Connections" below). The latest validated snapshot is stored on `hubs.stats_json` (a heartbeat without `stats` clears it); `hub_metrics(hub_id, ts, cpu, mem_pct, gpu_util, gpu_mem_pct, latency_ms)` keeps at most one point per Hub per 5 minutes (migration 0600_hub_stats.sql). Sample: `{"version":"1.8.2","profile":"home","updateChannel":"stable","health":{"ok":true,"services":[["voice","ok"]]},"stats":{"uptime_s":864000,"cpu_pct":37.5,"mem_used_mb":21000,"mem_total_mb":65536,"gpu":[{"name":"NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080","util_pct":62,"mem_used_mb":11000,"mem_total_mb":16384}],"services":[["voice","ok",86000]],"ai":{"mode":"local","models":[{"lane":"fast","name":"qwen3:8b","loaded":true}],"avg_latency_ms":840},"activity":{"requests_24h":120},"updates":{"latest_known":"1.9.0","last_result":"ok"}}}`
- GET /api/hubs -> `{hubs: [{id, name, edition, profile, version, updateChannel, remoteAccess, health: {ok, services}|null, lastSeen, createdAt, online, summary: {cpu_pct, mem_used_mb, mem_total_mb}|null}]}` (`online` = heartbeat within 15 minutes)
- GET /api/hubs/:id -> `{hub: {...list fields, stats: {...}|null}}` for owner or member of the Hub's account (also readable in a read-only view-as session); any other account's Hub, or an unknown id, is 404. GET /api/hubs/:id/metrics?range=24h|7d (default 24h; else 400) -> `{range, from, to, points: [{ts, cpu, mem_pct, gpu_util, gpu_mem_pct, latency_ms}]}`, bucket-averaged to at most 300 points. Pages: `/hubs/<id>` (static detail page); staff: `/support/hubs/<id>`, GET /api/support/hubs/:id (adds `accountId`, audited `support.hub.view`) and /api/support/hubs/:id/metrics, any account, read-only.
- PATCH /api/hubs/:id `{name?, updateChannel?, remoteAccess?}` -> `{hub}`; DELETE /api/hubs/:id -> `{ok}`
- GET /api/releases/latest?edition=mac|nvidia&channel=stable|beta -> `{edition, channel, version, manifestUrl, signatureUrl, signature, signatureScheme, namespace, sha256, releasedAt}`

Account (owner-only where noted)
- GET /api/account -> `{account: {id, createdAt}, members: [{id, email, role, status: "active"}], connectors: []}`. Connectors live on the Hub, so this is always an empty list.
- GET /api/account/export (owner) -> JSON of account, members, entitlement, hubs, orders, own passkey ids
- POST /api/account/delete (owner) `{confirm: "DELETE", cancelBilling?: true}` -> `{ok}`. Stripe is asked for non-terminal subscriptions and open checkout sessions: 409 `{error: "billing_active", subscriptions: [{id,status}], checkoutSessions: [id]}` and nothing is deleted, unless `cancelBilling` is true (they are then cancelled, verified terminal, and deletion proceeds). Stripe unreachable or cancellation unverifiable: 502, nothing deleted. Removes users, sessions, passkeys, hubs, billing links; hardware order rows stay (accounting) without the shipping address; the audit chain is append-only and keeps only ids and keyed IP hashes.
- GET /api/account also returns `invites: [{id, email, createdAt, expiresAt}]` (pending household invitations; owner only, otherwise empty).
- POST /api/account/members/invite (owner) `{email}` -> 201 `{invite: {id, email, expiresAt}}`; emails the invitee. 409 `already_member` | `already_invited` | `too_many_invites` (10 open); 502 `mail_failed`. DELETE /api/account/members/invites/:id (owner) cancels. Signing in never joins a household: GET /api/account/invitations -> `{invitations: [{id, inviterEmail, expiresAt}]}` (pending for the caller's email); POST /api/account/invitations/:id/accept (CSRF) joins as a member (only an empty own account is merged away; 409 `account_not_empty` / `already_member`; 404 otherwise); POST .../decline. DELETE /api/account/members/:userId (owner) removes a member (not the owner) and ends their sessions for the account.
- Joining: when someone signs in with the magic link/code using the invited address (invite open, 14 days), they become a `member` of that account. A person who has an untouched, just-created account of their own drops it and lands in the household. A person who already runs a real account (plan, Hubs, orders...) keeps it, and the invite stays pending (there is no account switching yet). There is no PATCH /api/account.

Static UI: every other GET is served from the `ASSETS` binding (portal/web build) with the same security headers.

Scheduled (hourly cron): prunes expired magic tokens, passkey challenges, sessions (expired or idle), hub pair codes, hub replay cache, hub rate counters and Hub metric points older than 8 days; flips manual grants (pilot, comp) past `ends_at` to `status = expired`, drops their pair codes, writes `entitlement_history` (kind `expired`) and an `entitlement.expired` audit row (actor `system:cron`); and seals any unsealed audit rows.
Support: proxy-free. The portal links to albena.ai/support.

## Connections (phase 1: visibility only, no remote control)
The portal shows which connectors a Hub has set up and whether they work. It never holds, sees or forwards a credential, token, URL, host or address, and it has no route that changes a connector.
- Heartbeat: optional `stats.connectors`, an array of at most 60 entries `{id, state, access, kind, label?, last_used_h?, verified?}`, strict (unknown keys are 400):
  - `id`: a catalog id (`portal/worker/src/connectors/catalog.ts`, mirrors the albena.ai connector catalog) or `"custom"`. Unknown ids are 400.
  - `state`: `connected` | `needs_attention` | `off`. `access`: `read` | `write` (`write` only for catalog entries that can write).
  - `kind`: `builtin` | `mcp` | `rest`. `custom` is always `mcp` or `rest`.
  - `label`: only when `kind` is `mcp` or `rest`; required for `custom`. 1 to 48 chars of letters, digits, space and `_ ( ) + & ' -`; rejected when it looks like an address (`@`, `://`, `www`, a dotted name ending in letters, an IPv4, `/`, `\` or `:`).
  - `last_used_h`: optional int 0 to 8760, whole hours since last use (coarse on purpose).
  - `verified`: optional boolean. `false` means the Hub has no health-check result for this connection yet (state is only "configured"); `true` means a stored health check backs the state. Absent (older Hubs) means unknown. The UI shows a "Connected — not yet verified" badge only for `state=connected` with `verified === false`. Strict boolean: anything else is 400. `GET /api/connectors` passes it through on the per-Hub entries and `custom` rows.
  - No duplicate catalog ids; no duplicate custom labels.
- Omitting `connectors` keeps the previous snapshot; `[]` clears it. The validated array is stored apart from stats in `hubs.connectors_json` (migration 0800_hub_connectors.sql); `GET /api/hubs/:id` returns it as `hub.connectors` (null when never reported) and staff `GET /api/support/hubs/:id` likewise.
- GET /api/connectors (owner, member, read-only view-as) -> `{categories: [{id,label}], catalog: [{id,name,category,auth: oauth_device|oauth_local|api_key|local|mcp,write,description,hubs: [{hubId,state,access,kind,last_used_h?}]}], custom: [{id:"custom",label,state,access,kind,last_used_h?,hubId}], hubs: [{id,name,online,lastSeen,reported}]}` for the caller's own account only. There are no write routes.
- GET /api/support/accounts/:id/connectors (staff, read-only) -> the same shape for any account; audited as `support.connectors.view`.
- UI: `/connectors` (catalog by category, search and filter, per-Hub status), a Connections panel on the Hub detail page and on the staff customer page. "Connect" is disabled until phase 2. Help: `portal/docs/connectors.md`.

## Customer lifecycle (staff area)
View-as starts with POST /api/support/view-as/start `{account}` (Access + CSRF; sets the read-only cookie, answers `{ok, redirect: "/"}`); there is no GET start, and every /api GET inside a view-as session is audited as `support.view_as.read` with its path. Reserving a Hub serial requires `publicKey` (400 `public_key_required`); serial pairing answers 400 for every failure. Wrong email codes are counted per address (10 in 24h -> 429 `code_locked_use_link`; the link still works). A new sign-in start invalidates older outstanding tokens for the address. Removing a passkey ends the user's other sessions. Stripe webhook redelivery of an event still `processing` (under 60s) answers 409. IPv6 clients are rate-limited per /64.

Staff pages live at `account.albena.ai/support/*` (customers list, `/support/customers/<id>`, `/support/invite`) and their API under `/api/support/*`. Both sit behind Cloudflare Access (add Access destinations `account.albena.ai/support/*` and `account.albena.ai/api/support/*`) and the worker re-checks the Access JWT plus `SUPPORT_ADMIN_EMAILS` on every request (deny by default). Customers and read-only view-as sessions are rejected (403 `forbidden`). Every write is a hash-chained audit row with actor `support:<email>`; browser writes need the usual `X-Requested-With` header.

Staff API (JSON):
- GET /api/support/accounts -> list with plan, status, source, endsAt. GET /api/support/accounts/:id -> `{account, users, entitlement, history, hubs, reservedHubs, orders, licenseKeys, notes, invites, audit}` (audited as `support.account.view`).
- POST /api/support/accounts `{email, name?, plan?...}` -> manual customer: user + owner account, no login. They sign in later with that email (normal magic sign-in) and find the plan in place. 409 `exists`.
- POST /api/support/accounts/:id/entitlement `{plan: byo|hub_mac|hub_nvidia|estate|pilot|comp, basePlan?, status: active|suspended, days?, ends_at?, maxHubs?, note?}`. `pilot` defaults to 30 days and 1 Hub; `comp` mirrors `basePlan` (required) at no charge; `maxHubs` overrides the plan's allowance. With an existing manual grant `plan` may be omitted (suspend, reactivate, extend). Returns the new entitlement; history kinds grant|extend|suspend|reactivate. Suspending drops pending pair codes.
- POST /api/support/accounts/:id/notes `{body}` (append-only, staff only). 
- POST /api/support/accounts/:id/orders `{edition: mac|nvidia, notes?}`; PATCH /api/support/orders/:id `{status, carrier?, tracking?, notes?}`: pending -> preparing -> shipped (carrier and tracking required) -> delivered; cancelled from pending or preparing. Manual orders only; the previous status is part of the UPDATE, so concurrent clicks cannot both win.
- POST /api/support/accounts/:id/reserved-hubs `{serial, edition, name?, publicKey?, days?}`; DELETE /api/support/reserved-hubs/:id (unused only).
- POST /api/support/accounts/:id/license-keys `{label?}` (BYO accounts) -> `{licenseKey}` shown once, only a peppered SHA-256 is stored; DELETE /api/support/license-keys/:id revokes.
- Invites: GET /api/support/invites; POST /api/support/invites `{email, plan?, basePlan?, days?, note?}`; POST /api/support/invites/bulk `{emails: [...], plan?...}` (max 50, a result per address); POST /api/support/invites/:id/resend (new link, old one dies; 60 s apart); DELETE /api/support/invites/:id revokes.

Invite flow (decision): the invite email carries `https://account.albena.ai/invite?token=<id>.<secret>`; only a SHA-256 of the secret is stored, it is single use and expires after 14 days. The `/invite` page asks the visitor to type the invited address and passes Turnstile; `POST /api/invite/accept {token, email, turnstileToken}` (public) then atomically consumes the invite, pre-creates user + account and (if the invite names a plan) the manual entitlement, and starts the ordinary magic sign-in to that address (same-browser cookie, 6-digit code on `/check-email`). Possessing the link therefore never signs anyone in; the mailbox does. Wrong addresses are counted (5 locks the invite until it is resent). An invite never replaces a live entitlement, and people who already have an account are refused at creation (409 `already_customer`).

The site admin waitlist (albena.ai/admin/waitlist) has an Invite button per row that opens `account.albena.ai/support/invite?email=...` prefilled; the portal never calls the site API.

## Rules
Stripe TEST mode only (sk_test via secret STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, whsec via STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET); never store card data; prices from Stripe Price IDs in vars. Same security headers/CSP as site worker. Tests with vitest + @cloudflare/vitest-plugin. No deploys, no remote resources — lead integrates and deploys.
